html:
On the 700 and 800 maps, Hindu states is a broad label for the many kingdoms of today's Rajasthan, Gujarat and Punjab, between the Arabs in Sindh and the powers of the Ganges plain.

In these years old clans were turning into the ruling houses later called Rajputs. The Gurjara Pratiharas rose from Mandore and Bhinmal. The Guhilas held Mewar, the Chahamanas Sambhar, and the Chavdas founded Anahilavada in Gujarat in the 740s. In Saurashtra the Maitrakas ruled until 776.

The great event was the arrival of Islam on the border. After the Arab conquest of Sindh in 712, Arab governors raided east. Indian kings, among them Nagabhata I and the Chalukyas of Gujarat, threw them back in the 730s, in what is often called the Battle of Rajasthan. The frontier then held for nearly three centuries. See also Rajput clans and small states.
